From: Ava Chen <ava@redwoodinference.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwoodinference.com>, Security Review Alias <security-review@redwoodinference.com>, Legal/Privacy Alias <legal-privacy@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jun 18, 2024 at 9:12 AM PT
Subject: Approval needed: External incident comms policy + post-incident summary timeline (Status page transparency upgrades)

Evelyn —

Need your approval today/tomorrow on the external incident comms policy for the status page transparency upgrades work.

Decision points to sign off:
1) Who can publish: oncall SRE + IC can publish incident updates using templates; resolved update requires SRE lead approval for Sev0/Sev1; post-incident summary requires SRE lead + Security/Legal consult only if it crosses disclosure boundaries.
2) Update cadence commitment (customer-facing):
   - Sev0/Sev1: first status page update within 15 minutes of declaring incident (or earlier if customer-facing impact is confirmed); updates at least every 30 minutes until stable mitigation is in place.
   - Sev2: first update within 30 minutes; updates at least every 60 minutes while impact is ongoing.
3) Post-incident summary SLA (customer-facing):
   - Sev0/Sev1: publish within 3 business days
   - Sev2: publish within 5 business days
   - Sev3: not published by default; can be provided to affected enterprise customers on request.

I’m including Security + Legal/Privacy aliases because we want a clean, reusable disclosure line (what we will never say publicly).

Docs:
- Attachment: External Comms Approval Policy - draft v3 (Google Doc)
- Attachment: Post-Incident Summary Template - customer-facing v2 (Google Doc)

If you’re aligned, please reply with “approved” + any changes. If not, call out the deltas and we’ll revise today.

Thanks,
Ava

—
Ava Chen
VP, Operations & Customer Experience
Redwood Inference


From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava@redwoodinference.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Security Review Alias <security-review@redwoodinference.com>, Legal/Privacy Alias <legal-privacy@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jun 18, 2024 at 9:26 AM PT
Subject: Re: Approval needed: External incident comms policy + post-incident summary timeline (Status page transparency upgrades)

+1 on urgency — this came up again this morning with an enterprise prospect (security review).

Two direct questions they asked:
- “Do you publish postmortems / RCAs publicly or only 1:1?”
- “If the status page says degraded, how do we know *what* is impacted (streaming vs embeddings vs region)?”

So I think the 3/5 business day commitment + component-level taxonomy are both strong answers, but we should be careful about not calling it a “postmortem” externally (they hear that as full internal doc).

Naomi

—
Naomi Feldman
Account Executive, Enterprise
Redwood Inference


From: Security Review Alias <security-review@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava@redwoodinference.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwoodinference.com>, Legal/Privacy Alias <legal-privacy@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jun 18, 2024 at 11:03 AM PT
Subject: Re: Approval needed: External incident comms policy + post-incident summary timeline (Status page transparency upgrades)

Thanks. Quick review notes (high level):

1) Please avoid language that commits us to disclosure of:
   - vulnerability details / exploit paths
   - exact vendor/provider incident identifiers
   - customer names or tenant-specific impacts

2) Strongly recommend the policy explicitly says:
   - “Root cause category” is OK (e.g., config change, capacity constraint, upstream provider issue), but do not include step-by-step reproduction details.
   - “Mitigation” should be phrased as customer-safe actions (retry/backoff, fallback model/region) vs operational specifics.

3) Summary SLA is fine as written, but add: “Timeline may be delayed if Security/Legal review is required.”

If you incorporate the above bullets, we’re good from the security side.

(Security Review Alias)


From: Legal/Privacy Alias <legal-privacy@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava@redwoodinference.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwoodinference.com>, Security Review Alias <security-review@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jun 18, 2024 at 11:41 AM PT
Subject: Re: Approval needed: External incident comms policy + post-incident summary timeline (Status page transparency upgrades)

Agree with Security.

Two additional redlines to include in the policy:
- No customer identifiers (names, unique request IDs, or “a Fortune 50 customer”) and no data volume specifics that could be used to infer customer usage.
- For upstream incidents: use “upstream provider” wording. Do not name the provider unless they have publicly posted an incident and our comms explicitly references their public link.

SLA note: fine to publish within 3/5 business days, but add “business days” explicitly in the external-facing language too.

(Legal/Privacy Alias)


From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwoodinference.com>, Security Review Alias <security-review@redwoodinference.com>, Legal/Privacy Alias <legal-privacy@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jun 19, 2024 at 8:07 AM PT
Subject: Re: Approval needed: External incident comms policy + post-incident summary timeline (Status page transparency upgrades)

Approved with 3 edits:

1) Terminology: externally call it “Post-incident summary” (not “postmortem” / “RCA”). Naomi’s point is right.

2) Update cadence: I’m comfortable with the targets, but we should phrase as guidance/standards rather than a contractual SLA unless it’s tied to an enterprise agreement. Suggested wording:
   - “We aim to post an initial update within X minutes…”
   - “We aim to provide updates at least every Y minutes while impact is ongoing…”

3) Add the Security/Legal disclosure bullets in the policy exactly as the aliases outlined.

Otherwise, ship it. Once it’s in Confluence, please make sure Support/CS gets the macro text aligned with the policy.

Evelyn

—
Evelyn Hart
Chief Product Officer
Redwood Inference


From: Ava Chen <ava@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Approval needed: External incident comms policy + post-incident summary timeline (Status page transparency upgrades)

Thanks all — incorporated changes and marked the drafts “Ready to publish”.

Edits made:
- Renamed everywhere to “Post-incident summary” (and added a one-line definition: customer-facing, not a full internal postmortem).
- Reframed cadence as “aim/target” language (explicitly not contractual unless in an SLA).
- Added disclosure “never share” bullets + upstream provider naming guidance.
- Added “may be delayed if Security/Legal review required” line to the summary SLA.

Naomi — once published, I’ll send you the approved external language for security questionnaires (“We publish post-incident summaries for Sev0/Sev1 within 3 business days…”) so it’s consistent.

Ava

—
Ava Chen
VP, Operations & Customer Experience
Redwood Inference
